question: Which gene is most frequently associated with acquired mutations in breast cancer?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "p53" -> "tumor suppressor gene" -> "frequent mutations in cancers" -> "common in breast cancer" -> 95%
CHAIN: "PTEN" -> "tumor suppressor gene" -> "mutations in various cancers" -> "less common in breast cancer" -> 60%
CHAIN: "BRCA-2" -> "DNA repair gene" -> "germline mutations" -> "hereditary breast cancer" -> 70%
CHAIN: "BRCA-1" -> "DNA repair gene" -> "germline mutations" -> "hereditary breast cancer" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Her2 / neu" -> "growth factor receptor" -> "overexpression in breast cancer" -> "not typically acquired mutations" -> 65%
analysis: The p53 gene is the most frequently associated with acquired (somatic) mutations in breast cancer. While BRCA1 and BRCA2 are well-known for hereditary breast cancer risk, p53 mutations are more common in sporadic cases. Her2/neu is often amplified in breast cancer but is not typically referred to as having acquired mutations in the same context as p53.
